{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZaa72g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDBu30", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 51, "title": "Implement 8253 mode-0 count-only rewrites and IRQ0 rearming", "body": "## Problem

DOS timer users cannot reliably replace or rearm a binary mode-0 count without writing another control word.

At baseline `4ed55ebf16c806ccf8be5f6cfbd6e8de0d81feca`, [Counter::write](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/4ed55ebf16c806ccf8be5f6cfbd6e8de0d81feca/src/devices.rs#L172) stores the first byte of a paired write without stopping an active counter. A completed rewrite schedules loading but never lowers OUT. Consequently, an interrupted old countdown can generate an unwanted IRQ0, and rewriting after terminal count cannot produce a subsequent terminal rise because [tick_mode0](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/4ed55ebf16c806ccf8be5f6cfbd6e8de0d81feca/src/devices.rs#L252) retains high OUT.

This is a distinct implementation gap explicitly excluded from completed Issue #49. Correct count replacement is a shared timer prerequisite across both supported machine profiles.

## Expected outcome

Implement count-only rewriting for binary mode 0, with GATE held high, on all three counters through both existing timer banks.

The hardware contract is:

- Writing a replacement count preserves the programmed mode and access format.
- A single-byte count write lowers OUT immediately. For LSB/MSB programming, the first byte immediately lowers OUT and stops counting; no countdown or terminal rise occurs while the second byte is missing.
- Completing the count schedules transfer on the next PIT clock. That clock loads without decrementing. Subsequent clocks decrement once each.
- Each completed replacement starts a new terminal-count lifecycle: OUT rises at zero, then stays high while counting continues modulo 65,536. Encoded zero represents 65,536.

Intel documents count replacement, paired-write stopping and clocked loading in the [8253/8253-5 Counter Loading and Mode 0 sections](https://web.cecs.pdx.edu/~mpj/llp/references/8253.pdf). Immediate first-byte OUT lowering and the separate load clock are explicit in [Intel 8254 Mode 0, page 10](https://www.scs.stanford.edu/23wi-cs212/pintos/specs/8254.pdf#page=10) and [NEC µPD71054 Table 5](https://www.meditronik.com.pl/doc/plus/upd71054c.pdf). These corroborate the shared mode-0 timing; other 8254 features are outside this Issue.

Only OUT0 low-to-high transitions request IRQ0. Falling or held OUT must not create a request. Intel describes edge-triggered recognition in the [8259A datasheet, page 17](https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse451/25wi/documentation/8259A.pdf#page=17). Preserve the repository's existing latched-request behavior when OUT falls; broader PIC electrical and spurious-interrupt modeling is outside scope.

## Context and reproduction

### Source-derived reproductions

Use the existing exact-PIT-clock `Clock` helper in `tests/pit.rs`; these sequences were inspected, not executed by the evaluator:

1. Program channel 0 with paired binary mode 0, count 4. Advance two PIT clocks: count is 3 and OUT is low. Write only replacement LSB 2, then advance four clocks. Expected: counting remains stopped and no rise occurs. Current code instead lets the old count reach terminal.
2. Independently program count 4 and advance five clocks to terminal. Rewrite count 2 without another control word. Expected samples after completion are `(2,L), (1,L), (0,H)`, with a new terminal rise. Current code retains high OUT.

Existing coverage does not establish this behavior. The [current guest probe](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/4ed55ebf16c806ccf8be5f6cfbd6e8de0d81feca/guest/pit_mode0.asm#L41) writes a fresh control word for every arming, and the existing Rust rearming check does likewise.

### Recorded project progress

PR #50 merged the fresh-programming mode-0 subset. The [Coordinator's validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/4ed55ebf16c806ccf8be5f6cfbd6e8de0d81feca/docs/validation.md#issue-49-8253-binary-mode-0-2026-10-23) reports 30 PIT passes, 190 native integration passes, and a final 74-test production-Wasm browser pass with zero skipped. Twelve mode-0 boots reportedly completed in 84,000 slots each. Earlier port conflicts and browser clock-setup failures are disclosed. Remote CI and independent review are not established by the supplied evidence. This evaluator performed source/diff inspection only.

All 26 fixed category scopes and statuses remain unchanged:

| Status | Categories |
| --- | --- |
| Partial | cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, keyboard, mouse, fdc, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, bios, lio, integration |
| Unimplemented | paging, fpu, rtc |
| Implemented, unverified | ide, grcg, pcm86 |

The supplied context lists no open Issues. This follow-up does not duplicate the fresh-programming behavior completed by #49.

### Focused scope and remaining work

Keep the implementation focused on mode-0 count replacement, pending-load cancellation, OUT lifecycle and existing IRQ0 integration. Preserve clock conversion, fractional remainder, batching and unrelated modes.

PIT remains partial after this Issue. External GATE/retriggering, modes 1/4/5, active mode-3 rewrites, BCD, divisor-1 mode-2/3 behavior, fuller latch/access sequencing and broader beeper acceptance remain outstanding; mode-0 audio remains unverified. This Issue does not add 8254 read-back commands or require general interleaved read/write sequencing. Protected execution, paging and basic FPU remain required project goals.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement the stated contract in original Rust. Add focused tests named with a `mode0_rewrite_` prefix in `tests/pit.rs`, including both reproductions above. Demonstrate that the focused reproductions and new guest probe fail against the stated baseline and pass with the implementation; record actual failure reasons.
- [ ] Cover all three channels and LSB-only, MSB-only and paired access forms. Include replacement values 1, 2, 65,535 and encoded zero where representable. Exercise replacement during countdown, immediately before terminal, after terminal and across later wraps. Verify exact count/OUT/edge traces, an indefinitely delayed second byte, latest complete replacement before loading, and a new partial pair superseding an older pending load. Do not assert undefined pre-load readback.
- [ ] Cover channel isolation, existing completed latch snapshots across replacement, fresh mode-word cancellation and reset during partial and pending-load states. Compare single-clock and irregular batched advancement across load/terminal/wrap boundaries, including zero advancement, fractional scheduler cycles and split versus unsplit `u32::MAX` advancement. Keep advancement bounded rather than iterating once per elapsed PIT clock.
- [ ] On VM and Ap, through both `0x71..0x77` and `0x3FD9..0x3FDF`, verify no IRQ0 from an incomplete replacement or falling OUT, retained existing PIC requests, one new request at replacement terminal count, and no repeats across later wraps. Preserve masking, acknowledgement, ISR/EOI and CPU IF/HLT/IRET behavior. Channels 1 and 2 must not request IRQ0.
- [ ] Add an original MIT source-built boot probe, preferably `guest/pit_mode0_rewrite.asm`, with offline preparation and a checked source/image/result manifest. Program mode 0 once, interrupt an active count with a deliberately delayed paired rewrite, verify no old-count IRQ during that delay, complete it, and rearm again after terminal using count writes alone. Check exactly one hardware IRQ0 per completed arming, ISR/EOI results and no repeated IRQ across a full subsequent wrap. Use bounded guest waits and preserve the existing probe unchanged. Do not read the timer between the two write bytes to depend on broader interleaving behavior.
- [ ] Run that identical image natively and through production-release Wasm, on both profiles before and after reset, at both browser URL roots. Require exact manifest-pinned result and guard bytes, PASS without FAIL, unchanged disk bytes, no core/browser errors and a fixed maximum of 2,000,000 scheduler slots per boot. Hosts may load, step, reset and inspect; they must not inject IRQs or write guest results. Retain assembly, license, reproduction command and hashes; acquire no commercial ROMs or guest software.
- [ ] Wire probe preparation into the existing CI flow. The Coordinator must run `cargo test --locked --test pit mode0_rewrite_`, `cargo test --locked --test pit`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `npm test`, following the [existing fixture and browser instructions](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/4ed55ebf16c806ccf8be5f6cfbd6e8de0d81feca/README.md#reproduce-the-checks). Preserve existing PIT/PIC/BIOS/CPU, DOS/apps/VM and game regression assertions and budgets. Use original or licensed fixtures with explicit provenance. Report exact commands, results, failures and any skips; do not weaken acceptance to obtain a pass.
- [ ] Update the bounded hardware contract and validation/provenance documentation. Keep PIT partial and retain every fixed inventory scope. Attribute execution evidence to its actual executor; limited probes and six-game reports do not establish full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
